summary: Connect a real 3 by 3 matrix to transformed basis arrows, vectors, and a reference shape using one shared mapping.
objective: Explain y = A x by showing how matrix columns determine the images of the standard basis and therefore every input vector.
example_prompts: Show how a 3 by 3 shear matrix moves the basis and a wireframe cube.
Let me edit a matrix and compare an input vector with its transformed image.

claims.statement: For a linear map written in standard coordinates with column vectors, A e_j is column j of A.
claims.scope: Real 3 by 3 matrices; the input and output standard bases are fixed.

claims.statement: The image of x is the combination of the images of the basis vectors with coefficients x_j.
claims.scope: A linear map R3 to R3, hence y = A x; no translation term.

source_refs.locator: 32.5, paragraph beginning Remember that any other vector

entities.name: Standard basis
entities.guidance: Keep reference e1, e2, e3 faintly visible; label each transformed arrow A e1, A e2, A e3.

entities.name: Input vector and image
entities.guidance: Show x and A x with distinct line treatments and numeric coordinates.

entities.name: Reference shape
entities.guidance: Use a wireframe cube or sparse lattice; map each vertex from its original coordinates.

state_contract.model: Finite real matrix A and vector x in a fixed, right-handed coordinate frame; column-vector convention.
state_contract.authority: One matrix value drives basis endpoints, geometry, vector output, and numeric labels. Keep original geometry immutable.
actions: Edit a matrix entry; reject non-finite values.
Select an authored example such as identity, shear, or axis collapse.
Reset A to identity and restore the input vector.

invariants: For each j, displayed A e_j matches column j of the matrix.
Every displayed transformed vertex comes from A times its original position, never cumulative frame-to-frame multiplication.
The origin stays fixed. Keep the displayed coordinate frame and units consistent.
Treat a singular matrix as a valid dimensional collapse; do not require an inverse to render it.
motion_guidance: If interpolating, explicitly use A(t) = (1-t)I + tA and derive every displayed value from A(t). Label t as transition progress, not physical time.
Intermediate matrices can be singular even for invertible endpoints; do not describe this blend as a rigid rotation.
Allow static before/after inspection and pause or scrub; keep the reference frame stationary.
creative_affordances: Choose translucent planes, luminous arrows, physical-looking rods, or a monochrome technical drawing while retaining coordinate and label meaning.
known_limits: This recipe describes an active linear map in fixed coordinates, not a passive change-of-basis lesson.
No determinant-volume, eigenvector, or SVD claims are included.
Numerical example was authored and checked arithmetically; no scene runtime or visual cross-check has run.
